Auto-delegation of all low-value repetitive tasks
One full day with zero emails or Slack messages
Immediate approval for any idea you propose
Remove all notifications from your phone & laptop

statements.text: Working longer hours makes you more productive
statements.explanation: Productivity drops after 6–7 hours due to fatigue.

statements.text: Multitasking helps you get more work done
statements.explanation: It reduces efficiency by up to 40%.

statements.text: Morning people are always more productive
statements.explanation: Depends on your chronotype (some are night owls).

statements.text: Checking email first thing in the morning is good
statements.explanation: It starts your day in reactive mode.
Busyness is activity. Productivity is impact.

statements.text: You need to be perfect before submitting work
statements.explanation: Done is better than perfect (80/20 rule).

statements.text: Team productivity improves with more meetings
statements.explanation: Too many meetings kill deep work.

statements.text: Using to-do lists makes you less productive
statements.explanation: Good to-do lists (with priorities) help a lot.

statements.text: Productivity is only about individual effort
statements.explanation: Team systems, communication & culture matter more.

items.hint: Founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs & Steve Wozniak in a California garage.
items.explanation: Designed by Ronald Wayne in 1976 featuring Sir Isaac Newton sitting under an apple tree!

items.hint: Original 1971 coffee house from Pike Place Market, Seattle.
items.explanation: The 1971 original logo featured a brown twin-tailed siren emblem!

items.hint: First crafted as "Brad's Drink" in 1893 in North Carolina.
items.explanation: Caleb Bradham renamed it Pepsi-Cola in 1898 and used this ornate red script logo!

items.hint: Launched as a podcast side-project at Odeo in 2006.
items.explanation: Designed by Noah Glass in 2006, the original name was spelled "twttr" with a green slime font!

items.hint: Launched by Kevin Systrom & Mike Krieger in October 2010.
items.explanation: The original 2010 icon was inspired by a vintage retro Polaroid camera!

items.hint: Danish wooden toy maker founded by Ole Kirk Christiansen in 1932.
items.explanation: Derived from Danish "leg godt" (play well), this 1936 ink stamp was used on wooden toys!

items.hint: First served at Jacob's Pharmacy soda fountain in Atlanta in 1886.
items.explanation: Before script lettering was adopted, Coca-Cola used a bold black slab serif font in 1886!

items.hint: Drive-in barbecue restaurant founded in San Bernardino, CA in 1940.
items.explanation: Speedee the chef was McDonald's original winking mascot before Ronald McDonald arrived in 1967!

items.hint: Search engine founded by Larry Page & Sergey Brin at Stanford in 1998.
items.explanation: The original 1998 logo featured a 3D GIMP font with a red exclamation point at the end!

items.hint: Software company founded by Bill Gates & Paul Allen in 1975 in Albuquerque.
items.explanation: The 1975 original logo used a grooved 1970s disco font and was spelled Micro-Soft!

items.hint: Oregon sportswear brand named after the Greek goddess of victory.
items.explanation: Graphic design student Carolyn Davidson created the iconic Swoosh logo in 1971 for just $35!

items.hint: Fast food chain founded by Harland Sanders in Corbin, Kentucky in 1952.
items.explanation: The original 1952 logo featured Colonel Sanders wearing his signature string tie and glasses!

items.hint: German sportswear company founded by Adolf Dassler in Herzogenaurach in 1949.
items.explanation: The 1949 original logo featured a spiked track running shoe suspended between two tall letter ds!

items.hint: Started as a London import business selling antique sea shells in 1891.
items.explanation: In 1904 Shell adopted a realistic black & white mussel shell drawing before adopting yellow & red colors!

items.hint: Japanese optical camera company founded in 1934.
items.explanation: Originally named Kwanon after the Buddhist Goddess of Mercy with a thousand arms!

items.hint: American automaker founded in Detroit, Michigan in 1903.
items.explanation: Henry Ford's original 1903 emblem used an ornate Victorian border before the blue oval in 1927!

items.hint: Formed from the merger of 3 computing-tabulating-recording companies.
items.explanation: Renamed International Business Machines in 1924, IBM adopted a globe emblem representing world trade!

items.hint: Handcrafted playing card company founded in Kyoto, Japan in 1889.
items.explanation: Fusajiro Yamauchi named it 任天堂 (Nin-ten-do), which roughly translates to "leave luck to heaven"!

items.hint: German carmaker founded in Wolfsburg in 1937.
items.explanation: The original 1939 VW emblem surrounded the interlocking V and W with a gear-tooth cog wheel!

items.hint: Founded in Jacksonville, Florida in 1953 as Insta-Burger King.
items.explanation: The 1954 original logo featured a cartoon monarch character sitting atop a sunburst backdrop!

items.hint: Flavored tortilla chip brand launched nationwide by Frito-Lay in 1966.
items.explanation: Derived from Spanish "doradito" (little golden thing), the 1966 original logo had a separate colored square box for each letter!

items.hint: Stackable potato chip brand developed by Procter & Gamble in 1967.
items.explanation: Julius Pringles (Mr. P) was created in 1967 featuring a rosy-cheeked head with a black mustache and red bow tie!

items.hint: Fast food submarine sandwich chain founded in Bridgeport, Connecticut in 1965.
items.explanation: Originally named Pete's Super Submarines in 1965, the 1968 logo introduced the iconic yellow and green text with arrow tips on S and Y!

items.hint: Dutch brewing company founded by Gerard Adriaan Heineken in Amsterdam in 1864.
items.explanation: The 1884 green oval bottle label introduced the red five-pointed star, representing the 4 elements of brewing plus mystery magic!

items.hint: Japanese automaker founded by Kiichiro Toyoda in Aichi Prefecture in 1937.
items.explanation: The company was originally named Toyoda (トヨダ). In 1936 they changed the name to Toyota (トヨタ) because it required 8 brush strokes, a lucky number in Japan!

items.hint: Online bookstore founded by Jeff Bezos in Bellevue, Washington in 1994.
items.explanation: The 1995 original logo featured a stylized letter "A" over a silhouette of the Amazon river!

items.hint: Open-source web project created at Netscape Communications in 1998.
items.explanation: Designed by street artist Shepard Fairey, the original 1998 mascot was a roaring red T-Rex dinosaur!

items.hint: Founded in 1865 as a single salmon-river wood pulp mill in Finland.
items.explanation: Named after the Nokianvirta river, Nokia's 1865 original logo featured a Finnish salmon fish emblem!

items.hint: Trading and grocery company founded in Taegu, Korea in 1938.
items.explanation: In Korean, "Samsung" means "Three Stars". The 1938 original logo was a grocery stamp with 3 stars!

items.hint: German luxury car manufacturer founded by August Horch in 1910.
items.explanation: Before the 4 interlocked rings, Audi's 1910 logo was an inverted black triangle with a numeral 1 on top!

items.hint: Evolved from Rapp Motorenwerke aircraft engine manufacturer in 1917.
items.explanation: The 1917 original BMW badge retained Rapp's outer ring shape with gold lettering and Bavarian flag colors!

items.hint: Automotive manufacturer founded in Hiroshima, Japan in 1920.
items.explanation: The 1936 triple-M logo represented the Hiroshima river streams and the initials of Mazda Motor Manufacturer!

items.hint: Fashion doll manufactured by American toy company Mattel, launched in 1959.
items.explanation: Ruth Handler created Barbie (named after her daughter Barbara) in 1959 with a classic magenta hand-drawn script logo!

items.hint: Video game brand created and produced by Sony Computer Entertainment in 1994.
items.explanation: Manabu Sakamoto designed the 3D polygon logo in 1994, featuring a red letter P standing vertically over a flat letter S shadow!

items.hint: American film and entertainment studio founded by four brothers in 1923.
items.explanation: Harry, Albert, Sam, and Jack Warner founded the studio in 1923, adopting the famous WB shield logo showing their Burbank studio lot photo!

items.hint: American luxury vehicle division of General Motors founded in Detroit in 1902.
items.explanation: Named after French explorer Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac, the original 1906 emblem was based on his noble coat of arms family crest!

items.hint: French car brand founded in 1810 as a coffee mill and bicycle manufacturing firm.
items.explanation: Engraver Justin Blazer designed the lion walking on an arrow mark in 1850 to represent the strength and flexibility of Peugeot steel saw blades!
